title: Forbearance of claims and settlement
summary: Compromise raises questions about the claimant’s belief as well as the underlying claim’s validity.
notes: Dyer uses Restatement § 74 to distinguish doubt about a claim from honest belief in a claim that proves invalid. The policy of encouraging settlements does not protect knowingly baseless demands. Fiege supplies a paternity-claim comparison, while the notes ask how litigation certification duties and other legal limits bear on promises not to sue. Settlement of uncertainty is itself a bargained-for benefit, but a court must still determine what was promised and surrendered.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 62–68. Open assigned page 62.
